referenceDefiningTraits: Notebook paper with horizontal rules and a vertical left margin rule.
Slightly skewed rectangles with uneven or doubled pencil-like edges.
Fine diagonal crosshatching creates tangible surface texture and patterned regions.
Bold sans lettering with marked size contrast, lightly irregular alignment and loose underline strokes.
Curved hand-drawn connectors, visible arrowheads and a folded-corner document silhouette.
The same construction remains recognizable in both light and dark references.

consistency.reason: The same notebook scaffold, doubled outlines, hatch texture, bold Japanese labels and palette roles hold across horizontal, compact, stacked, wide and portrait ratios. Ratio-specific topology and chair/clock/box icons make each composition distinct while maintaining the visual family.

character.reason: The defining notebook geometry, heavy type/light texture contrast and pencil-like surface remain recognizable. Expression is restrained: the reference’s asymmetrical tilted lettering, loose underlines, varied hatch coverage and prominent paper-document construction are reduced to more regular repeated card patterns. The required Japanese font and role colors are valid overrides, not character defects.

losses: Hatch coverage is largely standardized into strips instead of the reference’s varied, broad patterned regions.
Text and cards are more regularly aligned, reducing the reference’s loose pencil drawing rhythm.
Loose underline accents and the folded-page motif are not used; the motif is not a factual brief requirement.
batch.paletteObservation: Visible teal emphasizes completion/selectability and the usable undamaged path; orange warns on missing items or damage; waiting uses explicit wording and clocks. Exact hex values were not audited from source or pixel sampling.
batch.factualSummary: All required factual checks pass on visual evidence; no visible omissions, inventions or reversals.

fontUncertainty: The briefs prefer Noto Sans CJK JP. All Japanese glyphs appear readable with no visible missing-glyph boxes, but PNG-only review cannot establish the font actually rendered or whether fallback occurred.
scaleUncertainty: PNG dimensions include larger placement frames. Images were opened at native raster dimensions; the apparent artwork region corresponds to the stated target sizes, with 48 extra horizontal and 96 extra vertical pixels in each capture. Placement metadata and browser device scale were outside permitted evidence, so exact CSS-to-raster mapping was not independently verified.
scope: Only the dispatch, both reference PNGs, five capture PNGs, their common briefs/checklists and the common palette were read. No source, condition, prompt, run record, schemes/kits, coordinator scores or other runs were inspected.
